summary: Tantalum oxide thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) from TaCl5 and H2O at temperatures ranging from 80 to 500 °C. The films deposited at temperatures below 300 °C were predominantly amorphous, while those grown at higher temperatures were polycrystalline containing the phases Ta2O5 and TaO3. The oxygen to tantalum mass concentration ratio corresponded to that of Ta2O5 at all growth temperatures. The optical band gap was close to 4.2 eV for amorphous films and ranged from 3.9 to 4.5 eV for polycrystalline films. The refractive index measured at 550 nm increased from 1.97 to 2.20 with an increase in growth temperature from 80 to 300 °C. The films deposited at 80 °C showed low absorption with absorption coefficients of less than 100 cm-1 in the visible region.
